## Body

# Fence context before executable markers

A last-marker search does not establish that a marker opens an executable block. In #212, four lines consisting of an opening text-language fence, a literal pij opener, a send command and a closing fence are one quoted text example. Selecting the last pij-looking line nevertheless executes the example.

Track the enclosing fence before selecting the real trailing pij block. Apply the same eligibility cases to the transcript renderer: quoted code must not disappear as though it had been handed to the runner. Keep ordinary final blocks, permitted indentation and trailing-prose behavior distinct.

This was a source finding at `68ecd898a068ac4420b0defb2fd7445f7ccffafd`, not a local execution or a verified repair. See reviewer output `b909f2d409f57c323225bd9293f89fa5dd896367`, F001. A focused quoted-example case is enough; C34 does not require a new Markdown library, exhaustive inventory or mutation campaign.
